title: Societal Frameworks
description: Focuses on the sociological structures, demographics, and regional observations.

subtags.description: Customs specific to Andhras, Gaudas, and other regions, including variations in behavior, rituals, dress, food, and social expectations based on geographical and cultural context.
examples: Differences in marriage rituals between Andhra and Gauda regions
Regional dress styles and ornamentation
Variation in dietary habits and food restrictions

subtags.description: Rules based on Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra, including social hierarchy, duties, privileges, marriage restrictions, and behavioral expectations tied to caste identity.
examples: Restrictions on inter-caste marriage
Occupation assigned according to caste
Differences in ritual purity rules

subtags.description: Stages such as Student (brahmacarya), Householder (gṛhastha), and others, defining duties, behavior, and priorities appropriate to each phase of life.
examples: Discipline and celibacy during student life
Householder responsibilities including marriage and wealth
Transition from study to family life

subtags.description: Occupations, artisans, merchants, and organized guild systems that structure economic and professional life in society.
examples: Merchant guilds operating in cities
Artisan specialization such as jewelers or perfumers
Division of labor in urban environments

subtags.description: Social standing of sex workers, including their training, economic role, cultural refinement, and interactions with patrons and elites.
examples: Courtesans trained in music, poetry, and conversation
Financial relationships between courtesans and wealthy patrons
Role of courtesans in elite social life

subtags.description: Behaviors of kings and ministers, including etiquette, governance style, luxury, and expectations of conduct within elite circles.
examples: Conduct expected in royal courts
Display of wealth and refinement among elites
Ministerial etiquette and diplomacy

subtags.description: Social events and holidays that bring people together, including festivals, public celebrations, and communal gatherings.
examples: Spring festivals where social interaction increases
Public gatherings allowing courtship opportunities
Seasonal religious celebrations

subtags.description: Expected duties of men vs. women, including behavioral norms, responsibilities, and ideals associated with masculinity and femininity.
examples: Household responsibilities of a wife
Masculine ideals in courtship and leadership
Social expectations regarding modesty and conduct

subtags.description: Non-binary societal roles, including recognition and participation of individuals outside the male-female binary in social and intimate contexts.
examples: Roles of third-gender individuals in matchmaking or communication
Descriptions of alternative sexual identities
Participation in certain social or ritual contexts

subtags.description: Those outside the standard caste system, including foreigners and socially excluded groups, and their interaction with mainstream society.
examples: Interactions between caste society and outsiders
Perceived differences in customs and behavior
Restrictions on social or marital integration
